Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the ellipse shown above." :question/worked-solution "Since our ellipse is centered at $(2,-1)$ and has semiaxes $3$ and $4,$ its equation is given by

$$
\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-1))^{2}}{{4}^{2}}=1\,⟹\,\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16}=1.
$$

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{9}\right)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16}\right) & =0 \\ \frac{2(x-2)}{9}+\frac{2(y+1)}{16}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ \frac{y+1}{8}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{2(x-2)}{9} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{16(x-2)}{9(y+1)}\end{aligned}

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the ellipse shown above." :question/worked-solution "Since our ellipse is centered at the origin and has semiaxes $3$ and $1,$ its equation is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1\,⟹\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+{y}^{2}=1.
$$

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{16}\right)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4}\right) & =0 \\ \frac{2(x+1)}{16}+\frac{2(y-2)}{4}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ \frac{y-2}{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{x+1}{8} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{x+1}{4(y-2)}\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}\right) & =0 \\ 2x+\frac{2y}{9}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ \frac{2y}{9}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-2x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{9x}{y}\end{aligned}
